summary:
We developed a system which allows mission teams to pick any spot on the moon or mars' surface and returns an analog spot on earth's surface according to different dimensions we selected, using the data provided by NASA.
It is important because it will help mission teams find diverse locations in which to test equipment and methods before real missions.
details:
We developed a system which allows users to pick a spot on a 3D globe representing the moon or mars and shows the closest analog location on earth. This location is chosen based off of the similarity of dimensions we defined (Slope, Roughness, Relief, Ilumination).

We deployed the project using google cloud to the following URL: PANDA

It will help mission planners find more and diverse analog locations on earth.

This system will expand the opportunities for terrestrial testing and mission preparation by enabling mission planners and researchers to identify a wider range of Earth-based analog locations that closely resemble specific regions of the Moon or Mars. By facilitating the discovery of suitable testing environments, it will support more comprehensive validation of technologies, equipment, and operational procedures under realistic conditions before they are deployed in actual space missions.

Tools Used

Frontend: Developed using React in Typescript.

Libraries Used:

- react-globe.gl. Used for rendering the interactive 3D globes

- three. Used to avoid distortions when mapping the 2D maps onto the 3D globes.

Backend: Developed using FastAPI in Python.

Libraries Used:

- Rasterio. reads the giant elevation maps in small windows without blowing up memory, and rasterizes the Natural Earth coastline polygons into a land/ocean mask so we never return an analog in the middle of the sea.

We believe we were creative because we didn't find a perfect analog for only one site, but developed a system for finding good analogs for every site a mission may happen in.
